report.source_text: The patient received 2 g of ceftriaxone and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily. Initial treatment also included an infusion of 0.9% NaCl, 40 mg of esomeprazole once daily, 8 mg of ondansetron twice daily, and 1 g of paracetamol three times daily. Owing to the ECG findings, transcutaneous pacing was initiated at 40 mA with a rhythm maintenance rate of 70 bpm. A dopamine infusion was also administered, starting at 5 mcg/kgBW/minute and later titrated to 10 mcg/kgBW/minute until the systolic blood pressure exceeded 90 mmHg or the mean arterial pressure reached more than 65 mmHg.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old Asian woman from an endemic area presented with a 3-day history of worsening chest pain, fever (38.2°C), lethargy, anorexia, nausea, and intermittent headaches. On admission, she was hemodynamically unstable (BP 81/43 mmHg, HR 41 bpm) with clinical signs of jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, lung crackles, and anemia. ECG revealed total atrioventricular block (TAVB) with a junctional escape rhythm of 45 bpm. Chest X-ray showed cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio 0.52) with increased bronchovascular markings. Laboratory investigations confirmed Weil's disease with positive IgM and IgG anti-leptospirosis serology and positive microscopic agglutination test (MAT). Severe hepatorenal dysfunction was documented (creatinine 4.1 mg/dL, BUN 92 mg/dL, total bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL), along with anemia (Hb 10.3 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelets 98 × 10⁹/L), elevated transaminases (AST 102, ALT 65 IU/L), and elevated troponin I (361 ng/dL) indicating myocardial injury. Dengue serology was negative, ruling out dengue as an alternative diagnosis. Faine's score was 32, confirming severe Weil's disease. Treatment was initiated with ceftriaxone 2 g and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, supportive care (0.9% NaCl, esomeprazole, ondansetron, paracetamol), transcutaneous pacing at 40 mA with a maintenance rate of 70 bpm, and dopamine infusion titrated to 10 mcg/kgBW/minute. Despite aggressive management, the patient experienced cardiac arrest within 48 hours of admission. Despite ten cycles of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, return of spontaneous circulation was not achieved. The patient died within 48 hours of admission, with cardiogenic shock suspected as the cause of death.

final.final_diagnosis: Weil's disease (severe leptospirosis) complicated by total atrioventricular block (TAVB) and unstable hemodynamics
final.trajectory_summary: A 43-year-old Asian woman from an endemic area presented with a 3-day history of worsening chest pain, fever (38.2°C), lethargy, anorexia, nausea, and intermittent headaches. On admission, she was hemodynamically unstable (BP 81/43 mmHg, HR 41 bpm) with clinical signs of jaundice, hepatosplenomegaly, lung crackles, and anemia. ECG revealed total atrioventricular block (TAVB) with a junctional escape rhythm of 45 bpm. Chest X-ray showed cardiomegaly (cardiothoracic ratio 0.52) with increased bronchovascular markings. Laboratory investigations confirmed Weil's disease with positive IgM and IgG anti-leptospirosis serology and positive microscopic agglutination test (MAT). Severe hepatorenal dysfunction was documented (creatinine 4.1 mg/dL, BUN 92 mg/dL, total bilirubin 6.1 mg/dL), along with anemia (Hb 10.3 g/dL), thrombocytopenia (platelets 98 × 10⁹/L), elevated transaminases (AST 102, ALT 65 IU/L), and elevated troponin I (361 ng/dL) indicating myocardial injury. Dengue serology was negative, ruling out dengue as an alternative diagnosis. Faine's score was 32, confirming severe Weil's disease. Treatment was initiated with ceftriaxone 2 g and doxycycline 100 mg twice daily, supportive care (0.9% NaCl, esomeprazole, ondansetron, paracetamol), transcutaneous pacing at 40 mA with a maintenance rate of 70 bpm, and dopamine infusion titrated to 10 mcg/kgBW/minute. Despite aggressive management, the patient experienced cardiac arrest within 48 hours of admission. Despite ten cycles of cardiopulmonary resuscitation, return of spontaneous circulation was not achieved. The patient died within 48 hours of admission, with cardiogenic shock suspected as the cause of death.
